the_ladder: process #1 — THE GROUND LOOP. 'everything else can be brought down and the ground loop can still provide the pulse to bring it back up.'

process #2 — THE BUS, THE SHIMS, and related things. NOTE THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TICKET: shims are resident together in process 2, NOT one process per device. That is what makes presence work at all — the shim is always-on because it lives in a process that is always up, it can answer 'never booted' because no device process was ever spawned, and it can answer 'offline with last known' because it OUTLIVES the device it manages. CC's cast-time lean (build the process boundary for the librarian first as a proving ground) was solving a problem this layout does not have, and is withdrawn.
value.the_story_that_gives_the_why: 'There was a time before the ground loop idea where you'd spun up dozens of processes, deamons everywhere. it was faster to reboot than try and close them all. that's why the ground loop exists.' The ground loop is not a scheduler. It is the one process you are allowed to leave running, and it exists as the answer to a system nobody could shut down.
whys_in_his_words: 'this allows us to restart almost any part of the system for update without restarting the whole thing'
'a single component can crash hard, and the system can keep going'
'later, the system as a whole will respond to the resulting trouble ticket(s) for such an event without me' — the unattended-recovery aim, which is what the trouble lane is FOR
'process isolation for protection, for encpsulation. because that keeps everything as simple as possible.'

value.asked_by: Akien, 2026-08-11: 'you might want to ASK YOURSELF if we should do a pass for encapsulation adherence and appropriate boundries given it's been running as a unit?' — CC's answer, measured rather than agreed with: YES, and it goes BEFORE the split, not after.
value.finding_1_the_domains_are_not_devices: cairn/devices/db_domain/store.py and cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py declare NO Device or Shim class — they are MODULES, reached by direct function import. Every other thing on the roster subclasses BaseDevice; the two domains are the exception, and they are the two whose independent restartability Akien named as the point. Direct importers today (non-proof): bus/bus.py, librarian/trees.py, skill_block/counters.py and inference_domain/domain.py all take `from cairn.devices.db_domain import store`; librarian/live.py and intention_extractor/live.py take `from cairn.devices.inference_domain import domain, host`. So restarting the database proxy today means restarting everyone who imported it.
value.finding_2_the_gate_is_at_the_wrong_layer: import_sieve DOES enforce that only db_domain touches 5432 and only inference_domain dials the inference host — the owner-gate is real (Law 6). But it is an IMPORT-NAMESPACE door: it can say 'reach the DB only through this module', it cannot say 'only through this PROCESS'. So encapsulation is enforced at exactly the layer the process split makes insufficient. This is the CLAUDE.md residue ('a subprocess dials and imports nothing, and a dynamic import is invisible') coming due, and the ladder is what makes it due.
value.finding_3_the_base_reaches_up: cairn/tools/base/transitions.py — the emit chokepoint, inherited by EVERY device — imports FIVE other devices: build_inspector (x5), tester, orient, charter, chart. Four are deliberately lazy (function-local, commented 'keep import dependency-light'); line 122 is top-level (`from cairn.tools.charter import projector`). It is not accidental — the chokepoint must call the gates — but it means the layer UNDER every device reaches UP into five of them, which is the widest coupling in the system sitting at the bottom of it.
value.the_refinement_that_makes_the_pass_hones: AN IMPORT IS A PROXY FOR COUPLING, NOT COUPLING ITSELF. A module that imports `store` and calls one pure function is differently coupled from one holding a connection across a call. Reading the import graph and calling it the finding would repeat exactly the mistake that killed the census on mail-arrives-and-what-cannot-marks-itself (CC proposed reading class structure; Akien: ask the running device). So the pass reads WHAT CROSSES EACH EDGE — which functions, whether state or a live connection rides along, whether the caller survives the callee restarting — with the import graph as the MAP, not the measurement.
value.why_before_the_split_and_not_after: Akien's own story is the argument. Process isolation WITHOUT encapsulation adherence buys the worst of both: the daemon zoo that was faster to reboot than to shut down, now failing across a wire as well. If the boundaries do not hold, splitting into processes does not deliver 'restart one thing' or 'one component crashes and the system keeps going' — it delivers thirteen things that still cannot be restarted independently, plus IPC. The split's whole value IS the boundaries, so the boundaries are what must be measured first.

value.already_built: The chat pane RENDERS end to end (cairn/devices/web_server/render.py:147-172, transcript + form), the librarian DECLARES it (cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py:541-545), and a proof walks a POSTed utterance through the shim (proofs/test_web_server_chat.py). introspect() (cairn/tools/base/device.py:82) and active_page() (cairn/tools/base/shim.py:286) already give a floor-plus-declared-panes shape with ABSENT-WITH-REASON for an unwired pane — which is exactly the Scraps case (Akien's UU catch-all script device, given a chat window it could not honestly use, barking at anything that was not a slash command). bus.digest() already collapses a diagnostic channel to count+tail and REFUSES to collapse a record channel, which is the console pane's read arriving with its Law 7 tooth attached. This node is mostly COMPOSITION, not construction.
value.defects_found: (1) 'chat' is a channel that should never have existed, invented at TWO addresses — cairn/devices/web_server/render.py:165 hardcodes it in the form's hidden field, cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py:552 accepts only it — while the bus's falsifier reds on an unknown channel, so the one device with a real receive is structurally unreachable BECAUSE OF the invention. (2) The floor built at cairn/tools/base/shim.py:309-311 is two panes; it should be four. (3) BaseShim.deliver calls _ensure_device() BEFORE it checks for a receive, so it WAKES a device in order to discover the device cannot help — the sleep/wake model violated at the exact seam that exists to honour it. Found against code written 2026-08-10.
value.genuinely_absent: No pane kind 'console' exists anywhere in the tree. No shim spawns a process (no subprocess/Popen/fork). No verb set. No presence answer that works without waking the device. No CLI path to any device (bin/cairn dispatches to bin/cmd/<name> and there is no device fallback). The bus has no reply.
